small_guidance:
- The current scheme uses one program per output element with BLOCK_OC tiles; try inverting to one program per (N, pd, ph, pw) covering all OC at once (BLOCK_OC=16 fits OC=16 exactly), eliminating the OC grid dim and the oc_mask, and enabling reuse of x_val across all OC in registers.
- Reorder the inner loop so `ic` is the innermost reduction (load weight once per (kd,kh,kw,ic) as a [BLOCK_OC] vector and broadcast x_val scalar); also hoist the (id_,ih,iw) index/validity computation outside the `ic` loop since it doesn't depend on ic.
- Add autotune configs with BLOCK_OC=16 num_warps∈{1,2,4} num_stages∈{2,3,4}; current best likely under-utilizes due to tiny per-program work (only 8 spatial outputs × small OC). Consider tiling the 2×2×2 pooling window as a vectorized inner block rather than 3 static_range loops to encourage register reuse of the weight load.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, pooled-spatial tile, OC tile). For each pooled output, the 8 contributing conv-transpose outputs share the same input neighborhood; gather the relevant input slice once into shared/registers, then do a tl.dot against the weight tile (shape [IC*KD*KH*KW, OC]) and reduce the 2×2×2 window in-register before the epilogue. This converts the current scalar FMA loop into tensor-core matmul.
- Alternatively, flip to scatter-add: one program per (N, input voxel, OC tile) computes `x[n,ic,id,ih,iw] * W[ic,:,:,:,:]` outer product and atomically accumulates into the 8 pooled outputs it touches (divided by 8). With stride=2 padding=1 kernel=3, each input voxel writes to exactly 8 distinct pooled outputs with no atomic conflict across input voxels of different (id,ih,iw) parities — can be made atomic-free by coloring.
- Use channels_last (NDHWC) layout for both input and weight so the IC reduction axis is contiguous and loads coalesce; precompute and pass the OD/OH/OW dims rather than recomputing parity validity inside the kernel.
